short: Silent-EMG target transfer (M02) extends a 2016 DTW recipe; the open corpus scored by WER (M12) became the shared test bed. Headline 94% gain is closed-vocabulary, 20 clips, one evaluator.
position: The paper [@gaddy2020digital] changes two components: silent EMG learns audio targets transferred from a vocalized repetition (M02), and silent-EMG voicing gets an open 18.6-hour corpus scored by word error rate (M12). M02 is standard: Janke's 2016 dissertation already trained EMG-to-speech on silent EMG with DTW-transferred acoustic targets from audible recordings of the same sentences (§6.3.1) [@janke2016emg], so the claim to be first to train on silent EMG fails (Appendix, M02). M12 is standard: ASR scoring of EMG-to-speech output predates it [@janke2016emg], and its 68.0% WER fell to 42.2% a year later on the same split and recognizer [@gaddy2021improved] and to 11.89% with Whisper by 2026 [@lee2026gets]. The headline 94% reduction is a 67-word task with 20 clips per system and one evaluator (§4.1); open-vocabulary human WER falls 21% relative (95.1% to 74.8%; inference). CCA and the electrode ranking are single runs with no reported seed spread, and all 100 released test utterances come from one book.
